newsitem.title: USA: Motorola offers severance packages to workers.
newsitem.headline: Motorola offers severance packages to workers.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc said Saturday it has offered voluntary severance packages to thousands of employees in its semiconductor and automotive manufacturing plants as part of cost-cutting efforts after disappointing third-quarter earnings.

Margot Brown, director of external communications, said Motorola offered severance packages to about 6,000 employees at its semiconductor manufacturing plants in Austin, Tex., Irvine, Calif., and Research Triangle Park, N.C.
Employees at the plants received severance offer letters on Thursday and have one week to decide, Brown said.
Dan Rogers, the director of public affairs for Motorola's semiconductor sector, said the company would also shut down its non-manufacturing businesses at the three sites over the Christmas week.
The employees would be given holiday pay for two days and would have the option of taking vacation time or compensation time for the other three.
The employees in the manufacturing plants would work over Christmas based on demand for the products, which include microprocessors, microcontrollers, memory devices and telecommunications devices.
"They basically broke even in third quarter in semiconductors," Brown said. "They're making these adjustments."

The company said it also offered voluntary severance packages in September to employees in the company's automotive division in Albuquerque, N.M. and Schaumburg, Ill. A few hundred accepted the packages. Further details on the offer were not available.
"Automotive supplies some of our other businesses" which suffered stiff competition, a spokesperson said.

The semiconductor workers -- about 11,000 in Austin and less than 400 at each of the two other plants -- were offered one week's pay for each year of service up to 15 years, and two weeks' pay for each year after 15.
Brown declined to specify how many people the company hoped would accept the offer or if involuntary lay-offs were also being considered.
"There could be a reevaluation after getting the responses," Brown said. "They'll take it from there."
The package was offered to employees in non-manufacturing jobs in the semiconductor industry in July, and extended to those in the plants this week, Rogers said.

Earlier this month, the company reported a 58 percent drop in earnings compared with the third quarter last year and said it would take charges of "tens of millions of dollars" for cost-cutting measures, including personnel changes.
In July, the company terminated about 145 employees at its Austin plant -- Motorola's first lay-offs in more than a decade. Motorola has a total of 142,000 employees, Brown said.
